src/rankgenq.h

  1// Ranking extended to positions where the two players have different marker
  2// counts, so that any capture threshold q can be handled.
  3//
  4// ## Difference from rankgen.h
  5//
  6// With capture threshold one, a non-terminal position always has p markers on
  7// each side, so rankgen.h could fix the marker count. With threshold q the game
  8// continues after a capture, so positions with fewer markers are non-terminal
  9// too.
 10//
 11//   A player loses once q of their markers have been removed, that is, once the
 12//   count drops to p-q. Hence both counts lie between p-q+1 and p in every
 13//   non-terminal position, and the pair
 14//   (markers of the player to move a, markers of the opponent b) takes only
 15//   q^2 values.
 16//
 17// Each such pair (a,b) is called a **block**, and each block is given a
 18// contiguous range of indices. For q=1 there is a single block (p,p) and the
 19// numbering coincides exactly with rankgen.h.
 20//
 21// ## The blocks are layered
 22//
 23// Markers are only ever removed, so transitions between blocks go one way.
 24//
 25//   (5,5) -> (5,5) / (5,4) / (4,5)      ... for 5x5 with capture threshold two
 26//   (5,4) -> (4,5) / game over
 27//   (4,5) -> (5,4) / game over
 28//   (4,4) -> (4,4) / game over
 29//
 30// Solving the blocks in increasing order of the total marker count means the
 31// retrograde sweep only ever touches the block being solved. This is what
 32// determines the memory footprint.
 33#pragma once
 34#include <cstdint>
 35#include <cstdio>
 36
 37namespace rankgenq {
 38
 39static int NR = 5, NC = 5, NCELL = 25, NPIECE = 5, Q = 1;
 40static int PMIN = 5;                       // smallest marker count allowed in a non-terminal position = NPIECE-Q+1
 41static uint64_t BINOM[64][16];
 42static uint64_t SEC_OFF[8][8];             // first index of block (a,b)
 43static uint64_t SEC_SECOND[8][8];          // C(NCELL-a, b)
 44static uint64_t SEC_CNT[8][8];             // number of states in the block
 45static uint64_t TOTAL_CNT;
 46
 47inline uint64_t binom(int n, int k) {
 48  if (k < 0 || n < 0 || k > n || n >= 64 || k >= 16) return 0;
 49  return BINOM[n][k];
 50}
 51
 52inline int banCnt(int a) { return 4 * a + 1; }
 53
 54inline void init(int nr, int nc, int npiece, int q) {
 55  NR = nr; NC = nc; NCELL = nr * nc; NPIECE = npiece; Q = q;
 56  PMIN = NPIECE - Q + 1;
 57  for (int n = 0; n < 64; n++) {
 58    BINOM[n][0] = 1;
 59    for (int k = 1; k < 16; k++)
 60      BINOM[n][k] = (k > n) ? 0 : BINOM[n - 1][k - 1] + BINOM[n - 1][k];
 61  }
 62  // Lay out blocks with a smaller total marker count first; the retrograde
 63  // analysis can then solve them in this order.
 64  TOTAL_CNT = 0;
 65  for (int s = 2 * PMIN; s <= 2 * NPIECE; s++)
 66    for (int a = PMIN; a <= NPIECE; a++) {
 67      const int b = s - a;
 68      if (b < PMIN || b > NPIECE) continue;
 69      SEC_SECOND[a][b] = binom(NCELL - a, b);
 70      SEC_CNT[a][b] = binom(NCELL, a) * SEC_SECOND[a][b] * (uint64_t)banCnt(a);
 71      SEC_OFF[a][b] = TOTAL_CNT;
 72      TOTAL_CNT += SEC_CNT[a][b];
 73    }
 74}
 75
 76// --- The next four are defined exactly as in rankgen.h; they simply take the
 77// --- marker count k as an argument. ---
 78inline uint64_t maskToRank(uint64_t mask) {
 79  uint64_t r = 0; int i = 1;
 80  while (mask) {
 81    const int p = __builtin_ctzll(mask);
 82    mask &= mask - 1;
 83    r += binom(p, i); i++;
 84  }
 85  return r;
 86}
 87inline uint64_t rankToMask(uint64_t r, int n, int k) {
 88  uint64_t mask = 0;
 89  for (int i = k; i >= 1; i--) {
 90    int p = i - 1;
 91    while (p + 1 <= n - 1 && binom(p + 1, i) <= r) p++;
 92    mask |= 1ULL << p;
 93    r -= binom(p, i);
 94    n = p;
 95  }
 96  return mask;
 97}
 98inline uint64_t compress(uint64_t mask, uint64_t occupied) {
 99  uint64_t out = 0; int idx = 0;
100  for (int i = 0; i < NCELL; i++) {
101    if ((occupied >> i) & 1ULL) continue;
102    if ((mask >> i) & 1ULL) out |= 1ULL << idx;
103    idx++;
104  }
105  return out;
106}
107inline uint64_t expand(uint64_t cmask, uint64_t occupied) {
108  uint64_t out = 0; int idx = 0;
109  for (int i = 0; i < NCELL; i++) {
110    if ((occupied >> i) & 1ULL) continue;
111    if ((cmask >> idx) & 1ULL) out |= 1ULL << i;
112    idx++;
113  }
114  return out;
115}
116
117// Maps the forbidden move (from,dir) to 0..4a. "from" must hold a marker of
118// the player to move.
119inline uint32_t banRank(uint64_t cur, uint8_t ban) {
120  if (ban == 0xFF) return 0;
121  const int from = ban >> 2, d = ban & 3;
122  const uint64_t below = cur & ((1ULL << from) - 1);
123  return (uint32_t)(__builtin_popcountll(below) * 4 + d + 1);
124}
125inline uint8_t banUnrank(uint64_t cur, uint32_t br) {
126  if (br == 0) return 0xFF;
127  br--;
128  const int idx = br / 4, d = br % 4;
129  uint64_t m = cur;
130  for (int i = 0; i < idx; i++) m &= m - 1;
131  return (uint8_t)((__builtin_ctzll(m) << 2) | d);
132}
133
134inline uint64_t stateIndex(uint64_t cur, uint64_t opp, uint8_t ban) {
135  const int a = __builtin_popcountll(cur), b = __builtin_popcountll(opp);
136  const uint64_t pr = maskToRank(cur) * SEC_SECOND[a][b] + maskToRank(compress(opp, cur));
137  return SEC_OFF[a][b] + pr * (uint64_t)banCnt(a) + banRank(cur, ban);
138}
139
140inline void stateUnindex(uint64_t idx, uint64_t &cur, uint64_t &opp, uint8_t &ban) {
141  int a = 0, b = 0;
142  for (int s = 2 * PMIN; s <= 2 * NPIECE; s++)
143    for (int x = PMIN; x <= NPIECE; x++) {
144      const int y = s - x;
145      if (y < PMIN || y > NPIECE) continue;
146      if (idx >= SEC_OFF[x][y] && idx < SEC_OFF[x][y] + SEC_CNT[x][y]) { a = x; b = y; }
147    }
148  const uint64_t loc = idx - SEC_OFF[a][b];
149  const uint64_t pr = loc / banCnt(a);
150  cur = rankToMask(pr / SEC_SECOND[a][b], NCELL, a);
151  opp = expand(rankToMask(pr % SEC_SECOND[a][b], NCELL - a, b), cur);
152  ban = banUnrank(cur, (uint32_t)(loc % banCnt(a)));
153}
154
155}  // namespace rankgenq

src/solveq.cpp

  1// Complete retrograde analysis for capture threshold q on hole-free boards.
  2// The whole state space is indexed, and the states are split into blocks.
  3//
  4// ## Difference from solveidx.cpp
  5//
  6// solveidx only handles capture threshold one. There the game ends the moment a
  7// marker is removed, so every non-terminal position has p markers on each side
  8// and the marker count could be fixed in the numbering.
  9//
 10// With threshold q the game continues after a capture. A player loses once q of
 11// their markers have been removed, that is, once the count drops to p-q. Hence
 12// both counts are at least PMIN = p-q+1 in a non-terminal position, and the pair
 13// (markers of the player to move a, markers of the opponent b) takes q^2 values.
 14// The numbering is provided by rankgenq.h.
 15//
 16// ## Group the blocks by total marker count and solve the smallest first
 17//
 18// Markers are only ever removed, so the total s = a+b never grows. A move that
 19// captures nothing maps (a,b) -> (b,a) and keeps s; a capture or a self-removing
 20// move decreases s by one. Only blocks with the same s depend on each other.
 21//
 22//   s = 2p-2 : (p-1,p-1)                ... solved first
 23//   s = 2p-1 : (p,p-1) and (p-1,p)      ... one group of two
 24//   s = 2p   : (p,p)                    ... solved last
 25//
 26// Solving the groups in increasing order of s means each sweep only has to scan
 27// the group currently being solved.
 28//
 29// ## Running on 28 cores
 30//
 31// Within a sweep the states are independent, and a value changes only from
 32// UNKNOWN to WIN or LOSS, never back. So a thread that misses another thread's
 33// write simply reads the older value (UNKNOWN) and never settles a state too
 34// early; the missed update is picked up by the next sweep. The termination test
 35// is sound for the same reason: a sweep that makes no change performs no write,
 36// so every read in it is current.
 37//
 38// Packing values two bits at a time would break this, because four neighbouring
 39// states share a byte and concurrent writes would lose updates. Values are
 40// therefore stored **one byte per state**. For 5x5 with threshold two this grows
 41// the array from 6.60 GiB to 26.42 GiB, which buys an order of magnitude in speed.
 42//
 43// ## No counter array
 44//
 45// solveidx allocates cnt[] at one byte per state, but only writes it in the first
 46// pass and never reads it in the propagation loop, which recounts the children of
 47// each state every time. That was 16.11 GiB of pure waste, so it is not allocated
 48// here.
 49//
 50// ## How this is verified
 51//
 52// With q=1 the blocks collapse to the single block (p,p) and the indices from
 53// rankgenq coincide exactly with rankgen. So **reproducing the known values of
 54// solveidx with q=1 serves as a regression test**.
 55//
 56// The move logic is copied verbatim from src/solveidx.cpp.
 57//
 58// Build: g++ -O2 -std=c++17 -o build/solveq src/solveq.cpp
 59// Run  : ./build/solveq <height> <width> <markers per player> <q>
 60#include "rankgenq.h"
 61#include <chrono>
 62#include <cstdint>
 63#include <cstdio>
 64#include <cstdlib>
 65#include <cstring>
 66#include <vector>
 67#include <algorithm>
 68#include <thread>
 69#include <atomic>
 70
 71static int NR, NC, NCELL, NPIECE, Q, PMIN;
 72static const int DR[4] = {-1, 1, 0, 0};
 73static const int DC[4] = {0, 0, -1, 1};
 74static const uint8_t NO_MOVE = 0xFF;
 75
 76static inline bool inBoard(int r, int c) { return r >= 0 && r < NR && c >= 0 && c < NC; }
 77
 78// Applies a move. winner: 0 = game continues, 1 = the player to move removed an
 79// opponent marker, 2 = the player to move removed one of their own.
 80// The same logic as in solvepos.cpp / gapprobe.cpp (already verified).
 81static inline bool applyMove(uint64_t cur, uint64_t opp, uint8_t ban,
 82                             int from, int d,
 83                             uint64_t &ncur, uint64_t &nopp, uint8_t &nban,
 84                             int &winner) {
 85  if (!((cur >> from) & 1ULL)) return false;
 86  if (ban != NO_MOVE && ban == (uint8_t)((from << 2) | d)) return false;
 87  const uint64_t occ = cur | opp;
 88  const int dr = DR[d], dc = DC[d];
 89  int line[64], len = 1;
 90  line[0] = from;
 91  int rr = from / NC + dr, cc = from % NC + dc;
 92  int dest = inBoard(rr, cc) ? rr * NC + cc : -1;
 93  while (dest >= 0 && ((occ >> dest) & 1ULL)) {
 94    line[len++] = dest;
 95    rr = dest / NC + dr; cc = dest % NC + dc;
 96    dest = inBoard(rr, cc) ? rr * NC + cc : -1;
 97  }
 98  ncur = cur; nopp = opp;
 99  winner = 0;
100  int hole = dest;
101  for (int i = len - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
102    const uint64_t bit = 1ULL << line[i];
103    if (ncur & bit) {
104      ncur ^= bit;
105      if (hole < 0) winner = 2; else ncur |= 1ULL << hole;
106    } else {
107      nopp ^= bit;
108      if (hole < 0) winner = 1; else nopp |= 1ULL << hole;
109    }
110    hole = line[i];
111  }
112  if (winner != 0) { nban = NO_MOVE; return true; }
113  // If an opponent marker came to rest on the landing square, the move that
114  // pushes it back is the forbidden one.
115  nban = NO_MOVE;
116  if (dest >= 0 && ((nopp >> dest) & 1ULL)) nban = (uint8_t)((dest << 2) | (d ^ 1));
117  // **Swap the side to move.** A state always keeps the player to move in cur,
118  // so after a move the opponent becomes that player. Forgetting this builds a
119  // tree in which one side moves forever, and the retrograde analysis is
120  // meaningless.
121  const uint64_t t = ncur; ncur = nopp; nopp = t;
122  return true;
123}
124
125// Collapses a forbidden move that can no longer be played: if the square it
126// starts from holds no marker of the player to move, the restriction is vacuous.
127// This keeps one position from being counted under several forbidden-move values.
128static inline uint8_t killDeadBan(uint64_t cur, uint8_t ban) {
129  if (ban != NO_MOVE && !((cur >> (ban >> 2)) & 1ULL)) return NO_MOVE;
130  return ban;
131}
132
133enum : uint8_t { UNKNOWN = 0, WIN = 1, LOSS = 2 };
134
135int main(int argc, char **argv) {
136  NR = argc > 1 ? atoi(argv[1]) : 4;
137  NC = argc > 2 ? atoi(argv[2]) : 4;
138  NPIECE = argc > 3 ? atoi(argv[3]) : NC;
139  Q = argc > 4 ? atoi(argv[4]) : 1;
140  NCELL = NR * NC;
141  PMIN = NPIECE - Q + 1;
142  if (PMIN < 1) { fprintf(stderr, "q exceeds the number of markers\n"); return 1; }
143  rankgenq::init(NR, NC, NPIECE, Q);
144  const uint64_t TOTAL = rankgenq::TOTAL_CNT;
145
146  printf("board %dx%d, %d markers each, capture threshold %d\n", NR, NC, NPIECE, Q);
147  printf("markers when non-terminal : %d to %d (losing %d of them loses the game)\n", PMIN, NPIECE, Q);
148  printf("states                    : %llu\n", (unsigned long long)TOTAL);
149  printf("memory                    : %.2f GiB of values (one byte per state, no counter array)\n",
150         TOTAL / 1073741824.0);
151  fflush(stdout);
152
153  const auto t0 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
154  // One byte per state, so that a parallel write cannot corrupt its neighbours.
155  std::vector<uint8_t> value(TOTAL, 0);
156  uint8_t* const V = value.data();
157  auto getV = [&](uint64_t i) -> uint8_t { return V[i]; };
158  auto setV = [&](uint64_t i, uint8_t v) { V[i] = v; };
159
160  int NTH = (int)std::thread::hardware_concurrency();
161  if (const char* e = getenv("THREADS")) NTH = atoi(e);
162  if (NTH < 1) NTH = 1;
163  printf("threads                   : %d\n\n", NTH);
164  fflush(stdout);
165  // Splits [lo,hi) into NTH parts run in parallel. f(begin, end) writes only
166  // within its own range.
167  auto parallelFor = [&](uint64_t lo, uint64_t hi, auto&& f) {
168    std::vector<std::thread> th;
169    const uint64_t n = hi - lo;
170    for (int k = 0; k < NTH; k++) {
171      const uint64_t b = lo + n * (uint64_t)k / NTH, e = lo + n * (uint64_t)(k + 1) / NTH;
172      if (b < e) th.emplace_back([&f, b, e, k] { f(k, b, e); });
173    }
174    for (auto& x : th) x.join();
175  };
176
177  // Applies a move and returns the next position (with the side to move already
178  // swapped) together with any immediate outcome.
179  //   0 = illegal, 1 = ordinary child, 2 = playing it wins at once,
180  //   3 = playing it loses at once
181  auto step = [&](uint64_t cur, uint64_t opp, uint8_t ban, int from, int d,
182                  uint64_t &nc, uint64_t &no, uint8_t &nb) -> int {
183    int w;
184    if (!applyMove(cur, opp, ban, from, d, nc, no, nb, w)) return 0;
185    if (w != 0) {
186      // applyMove assumes capture threshold one and returns without swapping
187      // when it considers the game over. For q>=2 the game continues, so the
188      // swap is done here. A move that pushes a marker off the board cannot be
189      // undone in one move, so no forbidden move is recorded (nban stays
190      // NO_MOVE).
191      const uint64_t t = nc; nc = no; no = t;
192      nb = NO_MOVE;
193    }
194    // After the swap: nc holds the markers of the new player to move, no those
195    // of the opponent.
196    if (__builtin_popcountll(nc) < PMIN) return 2;   // the opponent has lost q markers: the mover wins
197    if (__builtin_popcountll(no) < PMIN) return 3;   // the mover has lost q markers: the mover loses
198    nb = killDeadBan(nc, nb);
199    return 1;
200  };
201
202  uint64_t nWin = 0, nLoss = 0;
203  int totalRounds = 0;
204
205  // Solve the groups in increasing order of the total marker count s. Blocks
206  // sharing an s occupy a contiguous range of indices.
207  for (int s = 2 * PMIN; s <= 2 * NPIECE; s++) {
208    uint64_t lo = UINT64_MAX, hi = 0; int nsec = 0;
209    for (int a = PMIN; a <= NPIECE; a++) {
210      const int b = s - a;
211      if (b < PMIN || b > NPIECE) continue;
212      lo = std::min(lo, rankgenq::SEC_OFF[a][b]);
213      hi = std::max(hi, rankgenq::SEC_OFF[a][b] + rankgenq::SEC_CNT[a][b]);
214      nsec++;
215    }
216    if (!nsec) continue;
217    printf("--- group with total marker count %d (%d blocks, %llu states) ---\n",
218           s, nsec, (unsigned long long)(hi - lo));
219    fflush(stdout);
220
221    // First pass: mark the immediate wins, and mark as a loss any position with
222    // no playable move once the immediately losing ones are excluded.
223    std::vector<uint64_t> tw(NTH, 0), tl(NTH, 0);
224    parallelFor(lo, hi, [&](int k, uint64_t b, uint64_t e) {
225      uint64_t w = 0, l = 0;
226      for (uint64_t i = b; i < e; i++) {
227        uint64_t cur, opp; uint8_t ban;
228        rankgenq::stateUnindex(i, cur, opp, ban);
229        int child = 0; bool immediateWin = false;
230        for (int from = 0; from < NCELL && !immediateWin; from++) {
231          if (!((cur >> from) & 1ULL)) continue;
232          for (int d = 0; d < 4; d++) {
233            uint64_t nc, no; uint8_t nb;
234            const int r = step(cur, opp, ban, from, d, nc, no, nb);
235            if (r == 0) continue;
236            if (r == 2) { immediateWin = true; break; }
237            if (r == 3) continue;               // an immediately losing move is never chosen
238            child++;
239          }
240        }
241        if (immediateWin) { setV(i, WIN); w++; }
242        else if (child == 0) { setV(i, LOSS); l++; }   // no move to play: a loss
243      }
244      tw[k] = w; tl[k] = l;
245    });
246    uint64_t gw = 0, gl = 0;
247    for (int k = 0; k < NTH; k++) { gw += tw[k]; gl += tl[k]; }
248    nWin += gw; nLoss += gl;
249    printf("  first pass: %llu immediate wins, %llu with no move   %.1f s\n",
250           (unsigned long long)gw, (unsigned long long)gl,
251           std::chrono::duration<double>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - t0).count());
252    fflush(stdout);
253
254    // Propagation. Only this group has to be scanned; the groups below are
255    // already solved.
256    int round = 0;
257    while (true) {
258      round++; totalRounds++;
259      std::vector<uint64_t> cw(NTH, 0), cl(NTH, 0);
260      parallelFor(lo, hi, [&](int k, uint64_t b, uint64_t e) {
261        uint64_t w = 0, l = 0;
262        for (uint64_t i = b; i < e; i++) {
263          if (getV(i) != UNKNOWN) continue;
264          uint64_t cur, opp; uint8_t ban;
265          rankgenq::stateUnindex(i, cur, opp, ban);
266          int unknownLeft = 0; bool anyLoss = false;
267          for (int from = 0; from < NCELL && !anyLoss; from++) {
268            if (!((cur >> from) & 1ULL)) continue;
269            for (int d = 0; d < 4; d++) {
270              uint64_t nc, no; uint8_t nb;
271              const int r = step(cur, opp, ban, from, d, nc, no, nb);
272              if (r == 0 || r == 3) continue;
273              if (r == 2) { anyLoss = true; break; }
274              const uint8_t v = getV(rankgenq::stateIndex(nc, no, nb));
275              if (v == LOSS) { anyLoss = true; break; }
276              if (v == UNKNOWN) unknownLeft++;
277            }
278          }
279          if (anyLoss) { setV(i, WIN); w++; }
280          else if (unknownLeft == 0) { setV(i, LOSS); l++; }
281        }
282        cw[k] = w; cl[k] = l;
283      });
284      uint64_t changed = 0;
285      for (int k = 0; k < NTH; k++) { nWin += cw[k]; nLoss += cl[k]; changed += cw[k] + cl[k]; }
286      printf("    sweep %d: %llu changed   %.1f s\n", round, (unsigned long long)changed,
287             std::chrono::duration<double>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - t0).count());
288      fflush(stdout);
289      if (!changed) break;
290    }
291  }
292
293  // the initial position
294  uint64_t F = 0, S = 0;
295  for (int c = 0; c < NPIECE && c < NC; c++) {
296    S |= 1ULL << (0 * NC + c);
297    F |= 1ULL << ((NR - 1) * NC + c);
298  }
299  const uint64_t start = rankgenq::stateIndex(F, S, NO_MOVE);
300  const uint8_t sv = getV(start);
301
302  if (const char *out = getenv("SAVE_VALUES")) {
303    FILE *fp = fopen(out, "wb");
304    if (fp) { fwrite(value.data(), 1, value.size(), fp); fclose(fp);
305      printf("values written to %s (%.2f GiB)\n", out, value.size() / 1073741824.0); }
306  }
307
308  printf("\n=== result ===\n");
309  printf("wins   : %llu\n", (unsigned long long)nWin);
310  printf("losses : %llu\n", (unsigned long long)nLoss);
311  printf("draws  : %llu\n", (unsigned long long)(TOTAL - nWin - nLoss));
312  printf("initial position: %s\n",
313         sv == WIN ? "Black wins" : sv == LOSS ? "White wins" : "draw");
314  printf("sweeps : %d\n", totalRounds);
315  printf("time   : %.1f s\n",
316         std::chrono::duration<double>(std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - t0).count());
317  return 0;
318}

src/solveqref.cpp

  1// Re-solves capture threshold q **sharing no code with solveq.cpp**.
  2//
  3// This is solve5x5ref.cpp (capture threshold one) generalised to threshold q.
  4// Only three things changed; the state handling, the normalisation and the
  5// retrograde analysis are untouched.
  6//
  7//   (1) applyMove: the position is kept, with the side to move swapped, even when
  8//       a marker is removed
  9//   (2) the outcome test is "fewer than PMIN markers" instead of "one removed"
 10//   (3) arguments: the third is now q and the fourth the state-count limit
 11//
 12// With q=1, PMIN = p and the behaviour is identical to the original solve5x5ref.
 13//
 14//
 15// ## Why a second implementation exists
 16//
 17// solveidx.cpp indexed the whole state space and found 5x5 to be a draw. But it
 18// carries its own numbering (rankgen.h) and its own applyMove. A checker built to
 19// the same design, verify5x5.cpp, would share both and so would not be an
 20// independent check.
 21//
 22// This file is instead built on solver6.cpp from the parent repository, which is
 23// already verified.
 24//
 25//   * state handling : hash table (no combinatorial ranking)
 26//   * scope          : **reachable states only**, not the whole space
 27//   * normalisation  : unified side to move, reflections, and collapsing of
 28//                      forbidden moves that can no longer be played
 29//   * retrograde     : the classical method, with an explicit list of predecessors
 30//
 31// Neither the way states are held nor the direction of the search matches
 32// solveidx, so a bug in one does not propagate to the other.
 33//
 34// ## Changes from solver6
 35//
 36// (1) The hash table now doubles automatically at a load factor of 0.5.
 37//     The original takes a fixed size in init and never resizes, so once the
 38//     number of states passes the capacity its linear probing degenerates and it
 39//     **burns CPU without making progress**. For 5x5 the reachable states run well
 40//     past a million, so this fix is essential.
 41//
 42// (2) Progress output was added. The run is long, and without it there is no way
 43//     to tell what is happening.
 44//
 45// src/solver6.cpp in the parent repository is untouched; it is only read.
 46//
 47// Build: g++ -O2 -std=c++17 -o build/solveqref src/solveqref.cpp
 48// Run  : ./build/solveqref <height> <width> <q> [state limit]
 49#include <chrono>
 50#include <cstdint>
 51#include <cstdio>
 52#include <cstdlib>
 53#include <cstring>
 54#include <vector>
 55
 56static int N = 4, M = 2, NCELL = 8;
 57static int Q = 1, PMIN = 2;   // PMIN = markers - Q + 1; below this the player has lost
 58
 59static const int DR[4] = { -1, 1, 0, 0 };
 60static const int DC[4] = { 0, 0, -1, 1 };
 61// how a reflection maps the directions
 62static const int FLIP_V[4] = { 1, 0, 2, 3 };   // vertical flip: U<->D
 63static const int FLIP_H[4] = { 0, 1, 3, 2 };   // horizontal flip: L<->R
 64
 65static inline bool inBoard(int r, int c) { return r >= 0 && r < N && c >= 0 && c < M; }
 66
 67static const uint8_t NO_MOVE = 0xFF;
 68
 69// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 70// State
 71//   cur : markers of the player to move
 72//   opp : markers of the opponent
 73//   ban : the forbidden move (source*4 + direction); NO_MOVE if none.
 74//         It records that playing this move would restore the previous board.
 75// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 76struct State {
 77    uint64_t cur, opp;
 78    uint8_t  ban;
 79    bool operator==(const State& o) const {
 80        return cur == o.cur && opp == o.opp && ban == o.ban;
 81    }
 82};
 83
 84// lexicographic comparison, used to pick the representative
 85static inline bool stateLess(const State& a, const State& b) {
 86    if (a.cur != b.cur) return a.cur < b.cur;
 87    if (a.opp != b.opp) return a.opp < b.opp;
 88    return a.ban < b.ban;
 89}
 90
 91// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 92// reflections
 93// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 94static inline uint64_t flipMask(uint64_t mask, bool h, bool v) {
 95    if (!h && !v) return mask;
 96    uint64_t out = 0;
 97    for (int r = 0; r < N; r++) {
 98        for (int c = 0; c < M; c++) {
 99            if (!((mask >> (r * M + c)) & 1ULL)) continue;
100            const int nr = v ? N - 1 - r : r;
101            const int nc = h ? M - 1 - c : c;
102            out |= 1ULL << (nr * M + nc);
103        }
104    }
105    return out;
106}
107
108static inline uint8_t flipMove(uint8_t mv, bool h, bool v) {
109    if (mv == NO_MOVE) return NO_MOVE;
110    int src = mv >> 2, d = mv & 3;
111    int r = src / M, c = src % M;
112    if (h) { c = M - 1 - c; d = FLIP_H[d]; }
113    if (v) { r = N - 1 - r; d = FLIP_V[d]; }
114    return (uint8_t)(((r * M + c) << 2) | d);
115}
116
117// the lexicographically smallest of the four reflections is the representative
118static inline State canonical(State s) {
119    State best = s;
120    for (int t = 1; t < 4; t++) {
121        const bool h = t & 1, v = t & 2;
122        State x{ flipMask(s.cur, h, v), flipMask(s.opp, h, v), flipMove(s.ban, h, v) };
123        if (stateLess(x, best)) best = x;
124    }
125    return best;
126}
127
128// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
129// Collapses a forbidden move that can no longer be played.
130//   If the square the forbidden move starts from holds no marker of the player
131//   to move, that move could not be played anyway. Normalising it to NONE merges
132//   states that differ only in history.
133//   This is the reduction that pays off most in the collaborator's implementation.
134// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
135static inline void normalizeBan(State& s) {
136    if (s.ban == NO_MOVE) return;
137    const int src = s.ban >> 2;
138    if (!((s.cur >> src) & 1ULL)) s.ban = NO_MOVE;
139}
140
141// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
142// Applies a move, from the point of view of the player to move.
143//   Returns true if the move is legal.
144//   nextState is the state after swapping the side to move (cur/opp exchanged).
145//   dropCur/dropOpp are the numbers of markers removed.
146// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
147static inline bool applyMove(const State& s, int from, int d,
148                             State& next, int& winner) {
149    // winner: 0 = game continues, 1 = the player to move wins, 2 = they lose
150    if (!((s.cur >> from) & 1ULL)) return false;
151    if (s.ban != NO_MOVE && s.ban == (uint8_t)((from << 2) | d)) return false;
152
153    const uint64_t occ = s.cur | s.opp;
154    const int dr = DR[d], dc = DC[d];
155
156    // Build the line to be pushed, starting with the marker being moved.
157    int line[64], len = 1;
158    line[0] = from;
159    int rr = from / M + dr, cc = from % M + dc;
160    int dest = inBoard(rr, cc) ? rr * M + cc : -1;
161    while (dest >= 0 && ((occ >> dest) & 1ULL)) {
162        line[len++] = dest;
163        rr = dest / M + dr; cc = dest % M + dc;
164        dest = inBoard(rr, cc) ? rr * M + cc : -1;
165    }
166
167    // Advance the line one square at a time, from its far end.
168    // If a marker leaves the board the game is decided; when several would fall,
169    // the colour of the nearer one decides the outcome.
170    uint64_t ncur = s.cur, nopp = s.opp;
171    winner = 0;
172    int hole = dest;                   // the empty square beyond the line (-1 means off the board)
173    for (int i = len - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
174        const uint64_t bit = 1ULL << line[i];
175        if (ncur & bit) {
176            ncur ^= bit;
177            if (hole < 0) winner = 2;  // own marker removed -> the player to move loses
178            else ncur |= 1ULL << hole;
179        } else {
180            nopp ^= bit;
181            if (hole < 0) winner = 1;  // opponent marker removed -> the player to move wins
182            else nopp |= 1ULL << hole;
183        }
184        hole = line[i];
185    }
186
187    // With capture threshold q the game continues after a marker is removed, so
188    // the position must not be discarded as it is for threshold one. A marker
189    // pushed off the board cannot be restored in one move, so no forbidden move
190    // is recorded.
191    if (winner != 0) {
192        next = State{ nopp, ncur, NO_MOVE };   // swap the side to move
193        return true;
194    }
195
196    // The forbidden move as seen by the next player to move.
197    // dest is the empty square at the head of the pushed line; moving the marker
198    // that came to rest there back again is the move that restores the previous
199    // board.
200    //
201    // Only the owner of that marker can play the reverse move, so the
202    // restriction matters only when the marker on dest belongs to the next
203    // player to move (nopp). Otherwise it would lapse on the next move, so it is
204    // collapsed to NO_MOVE, merging states that differ only in history.
205    // (This is the largest reduction in the collaborator's implementation.)
206    uint8_t back = NO_MOVE;
207    if (dest >= 0 && ((nopp >> dest) & 1ULL)) {
208        back = (uint8_t)((dest << 2) | (d ^ 1));   // d^1 swaps U<->D and L<->R
209    }
210
211    next = State{ nopp, ncur, back };   // exchange the side to move
212    return true;
213}
214
215// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
216// Hash table (open addressing)
217// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
218static inline uint64_t mix64(uint64_t z) {
219    z += 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ULL;
220    z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) * 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9ULL;
221    z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) * 0x94d049bb133111ebULL;
222    return z ^ (z >> 31);
223}
224
225struct Table {
226    std::vector<State>    keys;
227    std::vector<uint32_t> vals;    // 0 = empty, otherwise id+1
228    uint64_t mask;
229
230    uint64_t count = 0;
231    void init(uint64_t cap) {
232        uint64_t n = 1;
233        while (n < cap * 2) n <<= 1;
234        keys.assign(n, State{0, 0, 0});
235        vals.assign(n, 0);
236        mask = n - 1;
237        count = 0;
238    }
239    // Double the table once the load factor passes 0.5.
240    // The original solver6 does not do this; past capacity its linear probing
241    // degenerates and it burns CPU without making progress. Essential for 5x5.
242    void grow() {
243        std::vector<State> ok = std::move(keys);
244        std::vector<uint32_t> ov = std::move(vals);
245        const uint64_t n = (ok.size() ? ok.size() : 1) << 1;
246        keys.assign(n, State{0, 0, 0});
247        vals.assign(n, 0);
248        mask = n - 1;
249        for (size_t i = 0; i < ok.size(); i++) {
250            if (!ov[i]) continue;
251            uint64_t h = mix64(ok[i].cur ^ mix64(ok[i].opp) ^ ((uint64_t)ok[i].ban << 56)) & mask;
252            while (vals[h]) h = (h + 1) & mask;
253            keys[h] = ok[i]; vals[h] = ov[i];
254        }
255    }
256    // Returns the id if present; otherwise inserts and assigns newId.
257    uint32_t findOrInsert(const State& s, uint32_t newId, bool& isNew) {
258        if ((count + 1) * 2 > keys.size()) grow();
259        uint64_t h = mix64(s.cur ^ mix64(s.opp) ^ ((uint64_t)s.ban << 56)) & mask;
260        while (true) {
261            if (vals[h] == 0) {
262                keys[h] = s; vals[h] = newId + 1; isNew = true; count++;
263                return newId;
264            }
265            if (keys[h] == s) { isNew = false; return vals[h] - 1; }
266            h = (h + 1) & mask;
267        }
268    }
269    bool find(const State& s, uint32_t& id) const {
270        uint64_t h = mix64(s.cur ^ mix64(s.opp) ^ ((uint64_t)s.ban << 56)) & mask;
271        while (true) {
272            if (vals[h] == 0) return false;
273            if (keys[h] == s) { id = vals[h] - 1; return true; }
274            h = (h + 1) & mask;
275        }
276    }
277};
278
279int main(int argc, char** argv) {
280    if (argc >= 3) { N = std::atoi(argv[1]); M = std::atoi(argv[2]); }
281    Q = (argc >= 4) ? std::atoi(argv[3]) : 1;
282    PMIN = M - Q + 1;
283    if (PMIN < 1) { std::fprintf(stderr, "q exceeds the number of markers\n"); return 1; }
284    // The number of reachable states is not known in advance, so stop safely once
285    // the limit is passed. This keeps the process from exhausting memory and
286    // taking the machine down with it.
287    uint64_t stateLimit = (argc >= 5) ? std::strtoull(argv[4], nullptr, 10) : 0;
288    NCELL = N * M;
289    if (N < 2) { std::fprintf(stderr, "n must be at least 2\n"); return 1; }
290    if (NCELL > 63) { std::fprintf(stderr, "n*m must be at most 63\n"); return 1; }
291    if (NCELL * 4 > 255) { std::fprintf(stderr, "n*m*4 exceeds 255\n"); return 1; }
292
293    const auto t0 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
294
295    // initial position (the first player occupies the bottom row)
296    State init{ 0, 0, NO_MOVE };
297    for (int c = 0; c < M; c++) {
298        init.cur |= 1ULL << ((N - 1) * M + c);   // the player to move is the first player
299        init.opp |= 1ULL << c;
300    }
301    init = canonical(init);
302
303    Table table;
304    table.init(1 << 20);
305
306    std::vector<State>    states;
307    std::vector<uint8_t>  result;    // 0 = unknown, 1 = the player to move wins, 2 = they lose
308    std::vector<uint8_t>  degree;
309    // Predecessors could be generated by inverting the move that produces a
310    // state, avoiding an explicit list. But normalisation merges states, which
311    // makes that inversion awkward, so an explicit list of predecessors is kept
312    // instead; at 1/29 of the state count this is affordable.
313    std::vector<std::vector<uint32_t>> preds;
314
315    auto getId = [&](const State& s, bool& isNew) -> uint32_t {
316        const uint32_t id = (uint32_t)states.size();
317        const uint32_t got = table.findOrInsert(s, id, isNew);
318        if (isNew) {
319            states.push_back(s);
320            result.push_back(0);
321            degree.push_back(0);
322            preds.push_back({});
323        }
324        return got;
325    };
326
327    bool dummy;
328    const uint32_t initId = getId(init, dummy);
329
330    std::vector<uint32_t> settled;
331    uint64_t edgeCount = 0;
332
333    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
334    // Stage 1: enumerate the reachable states
335    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
336    bool aborted = false;
337    for (size_t qi = 0; qi < states.size(); qi++) {
338        if (stateLimit && states.size() >= stateLimit) { aborted = true; break; }
339        if ((qi & 0xFFFFF) == 0 && qi) {
340            std::printf("  enumerating: expanded %zu / known %zu\n", qi, states.size());
341            std::fflush(stdout);
342        }
343        const State s = states[qi];
344
345        bool hasWinMove = false;
346        uint32_t childBuf[64];
347        int childN = 0;
348
349        uint64_t t = s.cur;
350        while (t) {
351            const int from = __builtin_ctzll(t);
352            t &= t - 1;
353            for (int d = 0; d < 4; d++) {
354                State nx; int winner;
355                if (!applyMove(s, from, d, nx, winner)) continue;
356
357                // nx already has the side to move swapped: nx.cur holds the markers of
358                // the opponent of the player who just moved, nx.opp those of the mover.
359                if (__builtin_popcountll(nx.cur) < PMIN) { hasWinMove = true; continue; }
360                if (__builtin_popcountll(nx.opp) < PMIN) continue;   // a move that loses q of one's own markers is never chosen
361
362                nx = canonical(nx);
363
364                bool isNew;
365                const uint32_t nid = getId(nx, isNew);
366
367                // count the distinct children, for the degree
368                bool seen = false;
369                for (int i = 0; i < childN; i++)
370                    if (childBuf[i] == nid) { seen = true; break; }
371                if (!seen && childN < 64) {
372                    childBuf[childN++] = nid;
373                    preds[nid].push_back((uint32_t)qi);
374                }
375            }
376        }
377        edgeCount += childN;
378        degree[qi] = (uint8_t)childN;
379
380        if (hasWinMove)      { result[qi] = 1; settled.push_back((uint32_t)qi); }
381        else if (childN == 0) { result[qi] = 2; settled.push_back((uint32_t)qi); }
382    }
383
384    if (aborted) {
385        std::printf("\nenumeration stopped after reaching the limit of %llu.\n",
386                    (unsigned long long)stateLimit);
387        std::printf("states: at least %zu\n", states.size());
388        std::printf("result: ABORTED (undetermined; stopping early is not a draw)\n");
389        return 2;
390    }
391
392    const auto t1 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
393
394    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
395    // Stage 2: retrograde analysis
396    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
397    for (size_t si = 0; si < settled.size(); si++) {
398        const uint32_t v = settled[si];
399        const uint8_t rv = result[v];
400        for (uint32_t p : preds[v]) {
401            if (result[p] != 0) continue;
402            if (rv == 2) { result[p] = 1; settled.push_back(p); }
403            else if (degree[p] > 0 && --degree[p] == 0) { result[p] = 2; settled.push_back(p); }
404        }
405    }
406
407    const auto t2 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
408
409    uint64_t cw = 0, cl = 0, cd = 0;
410    for (size_t i = 0; i < result.size(); i++) {
411        if (result[i] == 1) cw++; else if (result[i] == 2) cl++; else cd++;
412    }
413
414    const uint8_t r0 = result[initId];
415    const char* verdict = (r0 == 1) ? "first player wins"
416                        : (r0 == 2) ? "second player wins" : "draw";
417
418    std::printf("========================================\n");
419    std::printf(" OSTLE complete analysis  n = %d, m = %d, q = %d  (hash table, reachable only)\n", N, M, Q);
420    std::printf("========================================\n");
421    std::printf("board       : %d x %d, %d markers each, capture threshold %d\n", N, M, M, Q);
422    std::printf("normalised  : side to move, reflections, lapsed forbidden moves\n");
423    std::printf("----------------------------------------\n");
424    std::printf("result      : %s\n", verdict);
425    std::printf("----------------------------------------\n");
426    std::printf("states      : %llu\n", (unsigned long long)states.size());
427    std::printf("non-terminal transitions: %llu\n", (unsigned long long)edgeCount);
428    std::printf("  mover wins: %llu\n", (unsigned long long)cw);
429    std::printf("  draws     : %llu\n", (unsigned long long)cd);
430    std::printf("  mover loses: %llu\n", (unsigned long long)cl);
431    std::printf("enumeration : %.2f s\n", std::chrono::duration<double>(t1 - t0).count());
432    std::printf("retrograde  : %.2f s\n", std::chrono::duration<double>(t2 - t1).count());
433    std::printf("total       : %.2f s\n", std::chrono::duration<double>(t2 - t0).count());
434    std::printf("========================================\n");
435    return 0;
436}

src/xcheckq.cpp

  1// An exact copy of solveqref.cpp with a position-by-position comparison against
  2// the values produced by solveq appended. The analysis itself is unchanged. Given
  3// LOAD_VALUES=<file>, each reachable representative is expanded into its orbit of
  4// four reflections and compared, one position at a time, with solveq's verdict
  5// looked up through rankgenq::stateIndex.
  6//
  7// Re-solves capture threshold q **sharing no code with solveq.cpp**.
  8//
  9// This is solve5x5ref.cpp (capture threshold one) generalised to threshold q.
 10// Only three things changed; the state handling, the normalisation and the
 11// retrograde analysis are untouched.
 12//
 13//   (1) applyMove: the position is kept, with the side to move swapped, even when
 14//       a marker is removed
 15//   (2) the outcome test is "fewer than PMIN markers" instead of "one removed"
 16//   (3) arguments: the third is now q and the fourth the state-count limit
 17//
 18// With q=1, PMIN = p and the behaviour is identical to the original solve5x5ref.
 19//
 20//
 21// ## Why a second implementation exists
 22//
 23// solveidx.cpp indexed the whole state space and found 5x5 to be a draw. But it
 24// carries its own numbering (rankgen.h) and its own applyMove. A checker built to
 25// the same design, verify5x5.cpp, would share both and so would not be an
 26// independent check.
 27//
 28// This file is instead built on solver6.cpp from the parent repository, which is
 29// already verified.
 30//
 31//   * state handling : hash table (no combinatorial ranking)
 32//   * scope          : **reachable states only**, not the whole space
 33//   * normalisation  : unified side to move, reflections, and collapsing of
 34//                      forbidden moves that can no longer be played
 35//   * retrograde     : the classical method, with an explicit list of predecessors
 36//
 37// Neither the way states are held nor the direction of the search matches
 38// solveidx, so a bug in one does not propagate to the other.
 39//
 40// ## Changes from solver6
 41//
 42// (1) The hash table now doubles automatically at a load factor of 0.5.
 43//     The original takes a fixed size in init and never resizes, so once the
 44//     number of states passes the capacity its linear probing degenerates and it
 45//     **burns CPU without making progress**. For 5x5 the reachable states run well
 46//     past a million, so this fix is essential.
 47//
 48// (2) Progress output was added. The run is long, and without it there is no way
 49//     to tell what is happening.
 50//
 51// src/solver6.cpp in the parent repository is untouched; it is only read.
 52//
 53// Build: g++ -O2 -std=c++17 -o build/solveqref src/solveqref.cpp
 54// Run  : ./build/solveqref <height> <width> <q> [state limit]
 55#include <chrono>
 56#include <cstdint>
 57#include <cstdio>
 58#include <cstdlib>
 59#include <cstring>
 60#include <vector>
 61
 62#include "rankgenq.h"   // solveq's numbering, used only for the comparison
 63
 64static int N = 4, M = 2, NCELL = 8;
 65static int Q = 1, PMIN = 2;   // PMIN = markers - Q + 1; below this the player has lost
 66
 67static const int DR[4] = { -1, 1, 0, 0 };
 68static const int DC[4] = { 0, 0, -1, 1 };
 69// how a reflection maps the directions
 70static const int FLIP_V[4] = { 1, 0, 2, 3 };   // vertical flip: U<->D
 71static const int FLIP_H[4] = { 0, 1, 3, 2 };   // horizontal flip: L<->R
 72
 73static inline bool inBoard(int r, int c) { return r >= 0 && r < N && c >= 0 && c < M; }
 74
 75static const uint8_t NO_MOVE = 0xFF;
 76
 77// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 78// State
 79//   cur : markers of the player to move
 80//   opp : markers of the opponent
 81//   ban : the forbidden move (source*4 + direction); NO_MOVE if none.
 82//         It records that playing this move would restore the previous board.
 83// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 84struct State {
 85    uint64_t cur, opp;
 86    uint8_t  ban;
 87    bool operator==(const State& o) const {
 88        return cur == o.cur && opp == o.opp && ban == o.ban;
 89    }
 90};
 91
 92// lexicographic comparison, used to pick the representative
 93static inline bool stateLess(const State& a, const State& b) {
 94    if (a.cur != b.cur) return a.cur < b.cur;
 95    if (a.opp != b.opp) return a.opp < b.opp;
 96    return a.ban < b.ban;
 97}
 98
 99// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
100// reflections
101// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
102static inline uint64_t flipMask(uint64_t mask, bool h, bool v) {
103    if (!h && !v) return mask;
104    uint64_t out = 0;
105    for (int r = 0; r < N; r++) {
106        for (int c = 0; c < M; c++) {
107            if (!((mask >> (r * M + c)) & 1ULL)) continue;
108            const int nr = v ? N - 1 - r : r;
109            const int nc = h ? M - 1 - c : c;
110            out |= 1ULL << (nr * M + nc);
111        }
112    }
113    return out;
114}
115
116static inline uint8_t flipMove(uint8_t mv, bool h, bool v) {
117    if (mv == NO_MOVE) return NO_MOVE;
118    int src = mv >> 2, d = mv & 3;
119    int r = src / M, c = src % M;
120    if (h) { c = M - 1 - c; d = FLIP_H[d]; }
121    if (v) { r = N - 1 - r; d = FLIP_V[d]; }
122    return (uint8_t)(((r * M + c) << 2) | d);
123}
124
125// the lexicographically smallest of the four reflections is the representative
126static inline State canonical(State s) {
127    State best = s;
128    for (int t = 1; t < 4; t++) {
129        const bool h = t & 1, v = t & 2;
130        State x{ flipMask(s.cur, h, v), flipMask(s.opp, h, v), flipMove(s.ban, h, v) };
131        if (stateLess(x, best)) best = x;
132    }
133    return best;
134}
135
136// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
137// Collapses a forbidden move that can no longer be played.
138//   If the square the forbidden move starts from holds no marker of the player
139//   to move, that move could not be played anyway. Normalising it to NONE merges
140//   states that differ only in history.
141//   This is the reduction that pays off most in the collaborator's implementation.
142// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
143static inline void normalizeBan(State& s) {
144    if (s.ban == NO_MOVE) return;
145    const int src = s.ban >> 2;
146    if (!((s.cur >> src) & 1ULL)) s.ban = NO_MOVE;
147}
148
149// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
150// Applies a move, from the point of view of the player to move.
151//   Returns true if the move is legal.
152//   nextState is the state after swapping the side to move (cur/opp exchanged).
153//   dropCur/dropOpp are the numbers of markers removed.
154// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
155static inline bool applyMove(const State& s, int from, int d,
156                             State& next, int& winner) {
157    // winner: 0 = game continues, 1 = the player to move wins, 2 = they lose
158    if (!((s.cur >> from) & 1ULL)) return false;
159    if (s.ban != NO_MOVE && s.ban == (uint8_t)((from << 2) | d)) return false;
160
161    const uint64_t occ = s.cur | s.opp;
162    const int dr = DR[d], dc = DC[d];
163
164    // Build the line to be pushed, starting with the marker being moved.
165    int line[64], len = 1;
166    line[0] = from;
167    int rr = from / M + dr, cc = from % M + dc;
168    int dest = inBoard(rr, cc) ? rr * M + cc : -1;
169    while (dest >= 0 && ((occ >> dest) & 1ULL)) {
170        line[len++] = dest;
171        rr = dest / M + dr; cc = dest % M + dc;
172        dest = inBoard(rr, cc) ? rr * M + cc : -1;
173    }
174
175    // Advance the line one square at a time, from its far end.
176    // If a marker leaves the board the game is decided; when several would fall,
177    // the colour of the nearer one decides the outcome.
178    uint64_t ncur = s.cur, nopp = s.opp;
179    winner = 0;
180    int hole = dest;                   // the empty square beyond the line (-1 means off the board)
181    for (int i = len - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
182        const uint64_t bit = 1ULL << line[i];
183        if (ncur & bit) {
184            ncur ^= bit;
185            if (hole < 0) winner = 2;  // own marker removed -> the player to move loses
186            else ncur |= 1ULL << hole;
187        } else {
188            nopp ^= bit;
189            if (hole < 0) winner = 1;  // opponent marker removed -> the player to move wins
190            else nopp |= 1ULL << hole;
191        }
192        hole = line[i];
193    }
194
195    // With capture threshold q the game continues after a marker is removed, so
196    // the position must not be discarded as it is for threshold one. A marker
197    // pushed off the board cannot be restored in one move, so no forbidden move
198    // is recorded.
199    if (winner != 0) {
200        next = State{ nopp, ncur, NO_MOVE };   // swap the side to move
201        return true;
202    }
203
204    // The forbidden move as seen by the next player to move.
205    // dest is the empty square at the head of the pushed line; moving the marker
206    // that came to rest there back again is the move that restores the previous
207    // board.
208    //
209    // Only the owner of that marker can play the reverse move, so the
210    // restriction matters only when the marker on dest belongs to the next
211    // player to move (nopp). Otherwise it would lapse on the next move, so it is
212    // collapsed to NO_MOVE, merging states that differ only in history.
213    // (This is the largest reduction in the collaborator's implementation.)
214    uint8_t back = NO_MOVE;
215    if (dest >= 0 && ((nopp >> dest) & 1ULL)) {
216        back = (uint8_t)((dest << 2) | (d ^ 1));   // d^1 swaps U<->D and L<->R
217    }
218
219    next = State{ nopp, ncur, back };   // exchange the side to move
220    return true;
221}
222
223// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
224// Hash table (open addressing)
225// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
226static inline uint64_t mix64(uint64_t z) {
227    z += 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ULL;
228    z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) * 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9ULL;
229    z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) * 0x94d049bb133111ebULL;
230    return z ^ (z >> 31);
231}
232
233struct Table {
234    std::vector<State>    keys;
235    std::vector<uint32_t> vals;    // 0 = empty, otherwise id+1
236    uint64_t mask;
237
238    uint64_t count = 0;
239    void init(uint64_t cap) {
240        uint64_t n = 1;
241        while (n < cap * 2) n <<= 1;
242        keys.assign(n, State{0, 0, 0});
243        vals.assign(n, 0);
244        mask = n - 1;
245        count = 0;
246    }
247    // Double the table once the load factor passes 0.5.
248    // The original solver6 does not do this; past capacity its linear probing
249    // degenerates and it burns CPU without making progress. Essential for 5x5.
250    void grow() {
251        std::vector<State> ok = std::move(keys);
252        std::vector<uint32_t> ov = std::move(vals);
253        const uint64_t n = (ok.size() ? ok.size() : 1) << 1;
254        keys.assign(n, State{0, 0, 0});
255        vals.assign(n, 0);
256        mask = n - 1;
257        for (size_t i = 0; i < ok.size(); i++) {
258            if (!ov[i]) continue;
259            uint64_t h = mix64(ok[i].cur ^ mix64(ok[i].opp) ^ ((uint64_t)ok[i].ban << 56)) & mask;
260            while (vals[h]) h = (h + 1) & mask;
261            keys[h] = ok[i]; vals[h] = ov[i];
262        }
263    }
264    // Returns the id if present; otherwise inserts and assigns newId.
265    uint32_t findOrInsert(const State& s, uint32_t newId, bool& isNew) {
266        if ((count + 1) * 2 > keys.size()) grow();
267        uint64_t h = mix64(s.cur ^ mix64(s.opp) ^ ((uint64_t)s.ban << 56)) & mask;
268        while (true) {
269            if (vals[h] == 0) {
270                keys[h] = s; vals[h] = newId + 1; isNew = true; count++;
271                return newId;
272            }
273            if (keys[h] == s) { isNew = false; return vals[h] - 1; }
274            h = (h + 1) & mask;
275        }
276    }
277    bool find(const State& s, uint32_t& id) const {
278        uint64_t h = mix64(s.cur ^ mix64(s.opp) ^ ((uint64_t)s.ban << 56)) & mask;
279        while (true) {
280            if (vals[h] == 0) return false;
281            if (keys[h] == s) { id = vals[h] - 1; return true; }
282            h = (h + 1) & mask;
283        }
284    }
285};
286
287int main(int argc, char** argv) {
288    if (argc >= 3) { N = std::atoi(argv[1]); M = std::atoi(argv[2]); }
289    Q = (argc >= 4) ? std::atoi(argv[3]) : 1;
290    PMIN = M - Q + 1;
291    if (PMIN < 1) { std::fprintf(stderr, "q exceeds the number of markers\n"); return 1; }
292    // The number of reachable states is not known in advance, so stop safely once
293    // the limit is passed. This keeps the process from exhausting memory and
294    // taking the machine down with it.
295    uint64_t stateLimit = (argc >= 5) ? std::strtoull(argv[4], nullptr, 10) : 0;
296    NCELL = N * M;
297    if (N < 2) { std::fprintf(stderr, "n must be at least 2\n"); return 1; }
298    if (NCELL > 63) { std::fprintf(stderr, "n*m must be at most 63\n"); return 1; }
299    if (NCELL * 4 > 255) { std::fprintf(stderr, "n*m*4 exceeds 255\n"); return 1; }
300
301    const auto t0 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
302
303    // initial position (the first player occupies the bottom row)
304    State init{ 0, 0, NO_MOVE };
305    for (int c = 0; c < M; c++) {
306        init.cur |= 1ULL << ((N - 1) * M + c);   // the player to move is the first player
307        init.opp |= 1ULL << c;
308    }
309    init = canonical(init);
310
311    Table table;
312    table.init(1 << 20);
313
314    std::vector<State>    states;
315    std::vector<uint8_t>  result;    // 0 = unknown, 1 = the player to move wins, 2 = they lose
316    std::vector<uint8_t>  degree;
317    // Predecessors could be generated by inverting the move that produces a
318    // state, avoiding an explicit list. But normalisation merges states, which
319    // makes that inversion awkward, so an explicit list of predecessors is kept
320    // instead; at 1/29 of the state count this is affordable.
321    std::vector<std::vector<uint32_t>> preds;
322
323    auto getId = [&](const State& s, bool& isNew) -> uint32_t {
324        const uint32_t id = (uint32_t)states.size();
325        const uint32_t got = table.findOrInsert(s, id, isNew);
326        if (isNew) {
327            states.push_back(s);
328            result.push_back(0);
329            degree.push_back(0);
330            preds.push_back({});
331        }
332        return got;
333    };
334
335    bool dummy;
336    const uint32_t initId = getId(init, dummy);
337
338    std::vector<uint32_t> settled;
339    uint64_t edgeCount = 0;
340
341    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
342    // Stage 1: enumerate the reachable states
343    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
344    bool aborted = false;
345    for (size_t qi = 0; qi < states.size(); qi++) {
346        if (stateLimit && states.size() >= stateLimit) { aborted = true; break; }
347        if ((qi & 0xFFFFF) == 0 && qi) {
348            std::printf("  enumerating: expanded %zu / known %zu\n", qi, states.size());
349            std::fflush(stdout);
350        }
351        const State s = states[qi];
352
353        bool hasWinMove = false;
354        uint32_t childBuf[64];
355        int childN = 0;
356
357        uint64_t t = s.cur;
358        while (t) {
359            const int from = __builtin_ctzll(t);
360            t &= t - 1;
361            for (int d = 0; d < 4; d++) {
362                State nx; int winner;
363                if (!applyMove(s, from, d, nx, winner)) continue;
364
365                // nx already has the side to move swapped: nx.cur holds the markers of
366                // the opponent of the player who just moved, nx.opp those of the mover.
367                if (__builtin_popcountll(nx.cur) < PMIN) { hasWinMove = true; continue; }
368                if (__builtin_popcountll(nx.opp) < PMIN) continue;   // a move that loses q of one's own markers is never chosen
369
370                nx = canonical(nx);
371
372                bool isNew;
373                const uint32_t nid = getId(nx, isNew);
374
375                // count the distinct children, for the degree
376                bool seen = false;
377                for (int i = 0; i < childN; i++)
378                    if (childBuf[i] == nid) { seen = true; break; }
379                if (!seen && childN < 64) {
380                    childBuf[childN++] = nid;
381                    preds[nid].push_back((uint32_t)qi);
382                }
383            }
384        }
385        edgeCount += childN;
386        degree[qi] = (uint8_t)childN;
387
388        if (hasWinMove)      { result[qi] = 1; settled.push_back((uint32_t)qi); }
389        else if (childN == 0) { result[qi] = 2; settled.push_back((uint32_t)qi); }
390    }
391
392    if (aborted) {
393        std::printf("\nenumeration stopped after reaching the limit of %llu.\n",
394                    (unsigned long long)stateLimit);
395        std::printf("states: at least %zu\n", states.size());
396        std::printf("result: ABORTED (undetermined; stopping early is not a draw)\n");
397        return 2;
398    }
399
400    const auto t1 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
401
402    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
403    // Stage 2: retrograde analysis
404    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
405    for (size_t si = 0; si < settled.size(); si++) {
406        const uint32_t v = settled[si];
407        const uint8_t rv = result[v];
408        for (uint32_t p : preds[v]) {
409            if (result[p] != 0) continue;
410            if (rv == 2) { result[p] = 1; settled.push_back(p); }
411            else if (degree[p] > 0 && --degree[p] == 0) { result[p] = 2; settled.push_back(p); }
412        }
413    }
414
415    const auto t2 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
416
417    uint64_t cw = 0, cl = 0, cd = 0;
418    for (size_t i = 0; i < result.size(); i++) {
419        if (result[i] == 1) cw++; else if (result[i] == 2) cl++; else cd++;
420    }
421
422    const uint8_t r0 = result[initId];
423    const char* verdict = (r0 == 1) ? "first player wins"
424                        : (r0 == 2) ? "second player wins" : "draw";
425
426    std::printf("========================================\n");
427    std::printf(" OSTLE complete analysis  n = %d, m = %d, q = %d  (hash table, reachable only)\n", N, M, Q);
428    std::printf("========================================\n");
429    std::printf("board       : %d x %d, %d markers each, capture threshold %d\n", N, M, M, Q);
430    std::printf("normalised  : side to move, reflections, lapsed forbidden moves\n");
431    std::printf("----------------------------------------\n");
432    std::printf("result      : %s\n", verdict);
433    std::printf("----------------------------------------\n");
434    std::printf("states      : %llu\n", (unsigned long long)states.size());
435    std::printf("non-terminal transitions: %llu\n", (unsigned long long)edgeCount);
436    std::printf("  mover wins: %llu\n", (unsigned long long)cw);
437    std::printf("  draws     : %llu\n", (unsigned long long)cd);
438    std::printf("  mover loses: %llu\n", (unsigned long long)cl);
439    std::printf("enumeration : %.2f s\n", std::chrono::duration<double>(t1 - t0).count());
440    std::printf("retrograde  : %.2f s\n", std::chrono::duration<double>(t2 - t1).count());
441    std::printf("total       : %.2f s\n", std::chrono::duration<double>(t2 - t0).count());
442    std::printf("========================================\n");
443
444    // ---- everything below is the only difference from solveqref ----
445    // The comparison is meaningful only on R, the set obtained by expanding the
446    // representatives into their four reflections: the reachable positions closed
447    // under reflection. solveqref never touches anything outside R, so the totals
448    // are not expected to agree.
449    const char* vf = std::getenv("LOAD_VALUES");
450    if (!vf) return 0;
451    rankgenq::init(N, M, M, Q);
452    const uint64_t TOTAL = rankgenq::TOTAL_CNT;
453    std::vector<uint8_t> value(TOTAL, 0);   // solveq stores one byte per state
454    {
455        FILE* fp = std::fopen(vf, "rb");
456        if (!fp) { std::fprintf(stderr, "cannot open %s\n", vf); return 1; }
457        const size_t got = std::fread(value.data(), 1, value.size(), fp);
458        std::fclose(fp);
459        if (got != value.size()) { std::fprintf(stderr, "size mismatch %zu != %zu\n", got, value.size()); return 1; }
460    }
461    auto getV = [&](uint64_t i) -> uint8_t { return value[i]; };
462
463    uint64_t gW = 0, gL = 0;
464    for (uint64_t i = 0; i < TOTAL; i++) { const uint8_t v = getV(i); if (v==1) gW++; else if (v==2) gL++; }
465    const uint64_t gD = TOTAL - gW - gL;
466
467    uint64_t R = 0, rW = 0, rL = 0, rD = 0, iW = 0, iL = 0, iD = 0, mism = 0;
468    int shown = 0;
469    for (size_t i = 0; i < states.size(); i++) {
470        const State s = states[i];
471        const uint8_t r = result[i];
472        State orb[4]; int no = 0;
473        for (int t = 0; t < 4; t++) {
474            const bool h = t & 1, v = t & 2;
475            State x{ flipMask(s.cur, h, v), flipMask(s.opp, h, v), flipMove(s.ban, h, v) };
476            bool dup = false;
477            for (int k = 0; k < no; k++) if (orb[k] == x) { dup = true; break; }
478            if (!dup) orb[no++] = x;
479        }
480        for (int k = 0; k < no; k++) {
481            const uint64_t id = rankgenq::stateIndex(orb[k].cur, orb[k].opp, orb[k].ban);
482            const uint8_t v = getV(id);
483            R++;
484            if (r==1) rW++; else if (r==2) rL++; else rD++;
485            if (v==1) iW++; else if (v==2) iL++; else iD++;
486            if (v != r) {
487                mism++;
488                if (shown < 20) {
489                    std::printf("  mismatch #%d idx=%llu cur=%llu opp=%llu ban=%u ref=%u idx=%u\n",
490                        shown, (unsigned long long)id, (unsigned long long)orb[k].cur,
491                        (unsigned long long)orb[k].opp, (unsigned)orb[k].ban, (unsigned)r, (unsigned)v);
492                    shown++;
493                }
494            }
495        }
496    }
497    State I{ 0, 0, NO_MOVE };
498    for (int c = 0; c < M; c++) { I.cur |= 1ULL << ((N - 1) * M + c); I.opp |= 1ULL << c; }
499    const uint64_t initIdx = rankgenq::stateIndex(I.cur, I.opp, I.ban);
500    const uint8_t initV = getV(initIdx);
501    const char* nm[3] = { "draw", "mover wins", "mover loses" };
502
503    std::printf("\n=== comparison with solveq (q=%d) ===\n", Q);
504    std::printf("states in the indexed space : %llu\n", (unsigned long long)TOTAL);
505    std::printf("  reachable R  : %llu (%.3f %%)\n", (unsigned long long)R, 100.0*(double)R/(double)TOTAL);
506    std::printf("  unreachable  : %llu\n", (unsigned long long)(TOTAL - R));
507    std::printf("representatives : %llu (orbit expansion %.4f x)\n",
508                (unsigned long long)states.size(), (double)R/(double)states.size());
509    std::printf("----------------------------------------\n");
510    std::printf("on R          ref(solveqref)      idx(solveq)\n");
511    std::printf("  mover wins : %16llu %16llu\n", (unsigned long long)rW, (unsigned long long)iW);
512    std::printf("  mover loses: %16llu %16llu\n", (unsigned long long)rL, (unsigned long long)iL);
513    std::printf("  draws      : %16llu %16llu\n", (unsigned long long)rD, (unsigned long long)iD);
514    std::printf("----------------------------------------\n");
515    std::printf("whole space idx : wins %llu / losses %llu / draws %llu\n",
516                (unsigned long long)gW, (unsigned long long)gL, (unsigned long long)gD);
517    std::printf("unreachable idx : wins %llu / losses %llu / draws %llu\n",
518                (unsigned long long)(gW-iW), (unsigned long long)(gL-iL), (unsigned long long)(gD-iD));
519    std::printf("----------------------------------------\n");
520    std::printf("initial position idx=%llu : ref=%s / idx=%s -> %s\n",
521                (unsigned long long)initIdx, nm[result[initId]], nm[initV],
522                (result[initId]==initV) ? "agree" : "DISAGREE");
523    std::printf("mismatched positions : %llu / %llu -> %s\n",
524                (unsigned long long)mism, (unsigned long long)R, mism==0 ? "all agree" : "MISMATCHES FOUND");
525    std::printf("========================================\n");
526    return (mism == 0 && result[initId] == initV) ? 0 : 3;
527}

src/countpos.cpp

  1// Counts the number of **positions** in the sense of the paper. It does not solve.
  2//
  3// In the Preliminaries a position is (current configuration, player to move,
  4// previous configuration). These correspond one to one with the edges of the game
  5// tree: one edge = one (previous configuration, current configuration) pair.
  6// Edges cannot be given a combinatorial ranking, so holding them explicitly would
  7// need a hash table; for 5x5 with capture threshold two that is 68 billion entries
  8// at over 20 bytes each, more than 1 TB, which does not fit in 256 GB.
  9//
 10// But **counting them needs no such table**. The outcome is already determined by
 11// the (configuration, player to move, forbidden move) encoding, since two
 12// positions that differ only in the previous configuration have exactly the same
 13// continuations. So the reachable states can be swept while the edges are counted
 14// one at a time and discarded, at constant memory.
 15//
 16// Only representatives modulo reflection are stored, so each representative is
 17// weighted by the size of its orbit to recover the true, unreflected count.
 18//
 19// If LOAD_VALUES points at a file saved by solveq, the positions are classified by
 20// the outcome of the position they lead to.
 21//
 22// Build: g++ -O2 -std=c++17 -o build/countpos src/countpos.cpp
 23// Run  : LOAD_VALUES=v.bin ./build/countpos <height> <width> <q>
 24//
 25// This is solve5x5ref.cpp (capture threshold one) generalised to threshold q.
 26// Only three things changed; the state handling, the normalisation and the
 27// retrograde analysis are untouched.
 28//
 29//   (1) applyMove: the position is kept, with the side to move swapped, even when
 30//       a marker is removed
 31//   (2) the outcome test is "fewer than PMIN markers" instead of "one removed"
 32//   (3) arguments: the third is now q and the fourth the state-count limit
 33//
 34// With q=1, PMIN = p and the behaviour is identical to the original solve5x5ref.
 35//
 36// ## Why a second implementation exists
 37//
 38// solveidx.cpp indexed the whole state space and found 5x5 to be a draw. But it
 39// carries its own numbering (rankgen.h) and its own applyMove. A checker built to
 40// the same design, verify5x5.cpp, would share both and so would not be an
 41// independent check.
 42//
 43// This file is instead built on solver6.cpp from the parent repository.
 44//
 45//   * state handling : hash table (no combinatorial ranking)
 46//   * scope          : **reachable states only**, not the whole space
 47//   * normalisation  : unified side to move, reflections, and collapsing of
 48//                      forbidden moves that can no longer be played
 49//   * retrograde     : the classical method, with an explicit list of predecessors
 50//
 51// Neither the way states are held nor the direction of the search matches
 52// solveidx, so a bug in one does not propagate to the other.
 53#include <chrono>
 54#include <cstdint>
 55#include <cstdio>
 56#include <cstdlib>
 57#include <cstring>
 58#include <vector>
 59
 60#include "rankgenq.h"
 61
 62static int N = 4, M = 2, NCELL = 8;
 63static int Q = 1, PMIN = 2;   // PMIN = markers - Q + 1; below this the player has lost
 64
 65static const int DR[4] = { -1, 1, 0, 0 };
 66static const int DC[4] = { 0, 0, -1, 1 };
 67// how a reflection maps the directions
 68static const int FLIP_V[4] = { 1, 0, 2, 3 };   // vertical flip: U<->D
 69static const int FLIP_H[4] = { 0, 1, 3, 2 };   // horizontal flip: L<->R
 70
 71static inline bool inBoard(int r, int c) { return r >= 0 && r < N && c >= 0 && c < M; }
 72
 73static const uint8_t NO_MOVE = 0xFF;
 74
 75// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 76// State
 77//   cur : markers of the player to move
 78//   opp : markers of the opponent
 79//   ban : the forbidden move (source*4 + direction); NO_MOVE if none.
 80//         It records that playing this move would restore the previous board.
 81// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 82struct State {
 83    uint64_t cur, opp;
 84    uint8_t  ban;
 85    bool operator==(const State& o) const {
 86        return cur == o.cur && opp == o.opp && ban == o.ban;
 87    }
 88};
 89
 90// lexicographic comparison, used to pick the representative
 91static inline bool stateLess(const State& a, const State& b) {
 92    if (a.cur != b.cur) return a.cur < b.cur;
 93    if (a.opp != b.opp) return a.opp < b.opp;
 94    return a.ban < b.ban;
 95}
 96
 97// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 98// reflections
 99// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
100static inline uint64_t flipMask(uint64_t mask, bool h, bool v) {
101    if (!h && !v) return mask;
102    uint64_t out = 0;
103    for (int r = 0; r < N; r++) {
104        for (int c = 0; c < M; c++) {
105            if (!((mask >> (r * M + c)) & 1ULL)) continue;
106            const int nr = v ? N - 1 - r : r;
107            const int nc = h ? M - 1 - c : c;
108            out |= 1ULL << (nr * M + nc);
109        }
110    }
111    return out;
112}
113
114static inline uint8_t flipMove(uint8_t mv, bool h, bool v) {
115    if (mv == NO_MOVE) return NO_MOVE;
116    int src = mv >> 2, d = mv & 3;
117    int r = src / M, c = src % M;
118    if (h) { c = M - 1 - c; d = FLIP_H[d]; }
119    if (v) { r = N - 1 - r; d = FLIP_V[d]; }
120    return (uint8_t)(((r * M + c) << 2) | d);
121}
122
123// the lexicographically smallest of the four reflections is the representative
124static inline State canonical(State s) {
125    State best = s;
126    for (int t = 1; t < 4; t++) {
127        const bool h = t & 1, v = t & 2;
128        State x{ flipMask(s.cur, h, v), flipMask(s.opp, h, v), flipMove(s.ban, h, v) };
129        if (stateLess(x, best)) best = x;
130    }
131    return best;
132}
133
134// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
135// Collapses a forbidden move that can no longer be played.
136//   If the square the forbidden move starts from holds no marker of the player
137//   to move, that move could not be played anyway. Normalising it to NONE merges
138//   states that differ only in history.
139//   This is the reduction that pays off most in the collaborator's implementation.
140// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
141static inline void normalizeBan(State& s) {
142    if (s.ban == NO_MOVE) return;
143    const int src = s.ban >> 2;
144    if (!((s.cur >> src) & 1ULL)) s.ban = NO_MOVE;
145}
146
147// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
148// Applies a move, from the point of view of the player to move.
149//   Returns true if the move is legal.
150//   nextState is the state after swapping the side to move (cur/opp exchanged).
151//   dropCur/dropOpp are the numbers of markers removed.
152// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
153static inline bool applyMove(const State& s, int from, int d,
154                             State& next, int& winner) {
155    // winner: 0 = game continues, 1 = the player to move wins, 2 = they lose
156    if (!((s.cur >> from) & 1ULL)) return false;
157    if (s.ban != NO_MOVE && s.ban == (uint8_t)((from << 2) | d)) return false;
158
159    const uint64_t occ = s.cur | s.opp;
160    const int dr = DR[d], dc = DC[d];
161
162    // Build the line to be pushed, starting with the marker being moved.
163    int line[64], len = 1;
164    line[0] = from;
165    int rr = from / M + dr, cc = from % M + dc;
166    int dest = inBoard(rr, cc) ? rr * M + cc : -1;
167    while (dest >= 0 && ((occ >> dest) & 1ULL)) {
168        line[len++] = dest;
169        rr = dest / M + dr; cc = dest % M + dc;
170        dest = inBoard(rr, cc) ? rr * M + cc : -1;
171    }
172
173    // Advance the line one square at a time, from its far end.
174    // If a marker leaves the board the game is decided; when several would fall,
175    // the colour of the nearer one decides the outcome.
176    uint64_t ncur = s.cur, nopp = s.opp;
177    winner = 0;
178    int hole = dest;                   // the empty square beyond the line (-1 means off the board)
179    for (int i = len - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
180        const uint64_t bit = 1ULL << line[i];
181        if (ncur & bit) {
182            ncur ^= bit;
183            if (hole < 0) winner = 2;  // own marker removed -> the player to move loses
184            else ncur |= 1ULL << hole;
185        } else {
186            nopp ^= bit;
187            if (hole < 0) winner = 1;  // opponent marker removed -> the player to move wins
188            else nopp |= 1ULL << hole;
189        }
190        hole = line[i];
191    }
192
193    // With capture threshold q the game continues after a marker is removed, so
194    // the position must not be discarded as it is for threshold one. A marker
195    // pushed off the board cannot be restored in one move, so no forbidden move
196    // is recorded.
197    if (winner != 0) {
198        next = State{ nopp, ncur, NO_MOVE };   // swap the side to move
199        return true;
200    }
201
202    // The forbidden move as seen by the next player to move.
203    // dest is the empty square at the head of the pushed line; moving the marker
204    // that came to rest there back again is the move that restores the previous
205    // board.
206    //
207    // Only the owner of that marker can play the reverse move, so the
208    // restriction matters only when the marker on dest belongs to the next
209    // player to move (nopp). Otherwise it would lapse on the next move, so it is
210    // collapsed to NO_MOVE, merging states that differ only in history.
211    // (This is the largest reduction in the collaborator's implementation.)
212    uint8_t back = NO_MOVE;
213    if (dest >= 0 && ((nopp >> dest) & 1ULL)) {
214        back = (uint8_t)((dest << 2) | (d ^ 1));   // d^1 swaps U<->D and L<->R
215    }
216
217    next = State{ nopp, ncur, back };   // exchange the side to move
218    return true;
219}
220
221// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
222// Hash table (open addressing)
223// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
224static inline uint64_t mix64(uint64_t z) {
225    z += 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ULL;
226    z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) * 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9ULL;
227    z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) * 0x94d049bb133111ebULL;
228    return z ^ (z >> 31);
229}
230
231struct Table {
232    std::vector<State>    keys;
233    std::vector<uint32_t> vals;    // 0 = empty, otherwise id+1
234    uint64_t mask;
235
236    uint64_t count = 0;
237    void init(uint64_t cap) {
238        uint64_t n = 1;
239        while (n < cap * 2) n <<= 1;
240        keys.assign(n, State{0, 0, 0});
241        vals.assign(n, 0);
242        mask = n - 1;
243        count = 0;
244    }
245    // Double the table once the load factor passes 0.5.
246    // The original solver6 does not do this; past capacity its linear probing
247    // degenerates and it burns CPU without making progress. Essential for 5x5.
248    void grow() {
249        std::vector<State> ok = std::move(keys);
250        std::vector<uint32_t> ov = std::move(vals);
251        const uint64_t n = (ok.size() ? ok.size() : 1) << 1;
252        keys.assign(n, State{0, 0, 0});
253        vals.assign(n, 0);
254        mask = n - 1;
255        for (size_t i = 0; i < ok.size(); i++) {
256            if (!ov[i]) continue;
257            uint64_t h = mix64(ok[i].cur ^ mix64(ok[i].opp) ^ ((uint64_t)ok[i].ban << 56)) & mask;
258            while (vals[h]) h = (h + 1) & mask;
259            keys[h] = ok[i]; vals[h] = ov[i];
260        }
261    }
262    // Returns the id if present; otherwise inserts and assigns newId.
263    uint32_t findOrInsert(const State& s, uint32_t newId, bool& isNew) {
264        if ((count + 1) * 2 > keys.size()) grow();
265        uint64_t h = mix64(s.cur ^ mix64(s.opp) ^ ((uint64_t)s.ban << 56)) & mask;
266        while (true) {
267            if (vals[h] == 0) {
268                keys[h] = s; vals[h] = newId + 1; isNew = true; count++;
269                return newId;
270            }
271            if (keys[h] == s) { isNew = false; return vals[h] - 1; }
272            h = (h + 1) & mask;
273        }
274    }
275    bool find(const State& s, uint32_t& id) const {
276        uint64_t h = mix64(s.cur ^ mix64(s.opp) ^ ((uint64_t)s.ban << 56)) & mask;
277        while (true) {
278            if (vals[h] == 0) return false;
279            if (keys[h] == s) { id = vals[h] - 1; return true; }
280            h = (h + 1) & mask;
281        }
282    }
283};
284
285int main(int argc, char** argv) {
286    if (argc >= 3) { N = std::atoi(argv[1]); M = std::atoi(argv[2]); }
287    Q = (argc >= 4) ? std::atoi(argv[3]) : 1;
288    PMIN = M - Q + 1;
289    if (PMIN < 1) { std::fprintf(stderr, "q exceeds the number of markers\n"); return 1; }
290    // The number of reachable states is not known in advance, so stop safely once
291    // the limit is passed. This keeps the process from exhausting memory and
292    // taking the machine down with it.
293    uint64_t stateLimit = (argc >= 5) ? std::strtoull(argv[4], nullptr, 10) : 0;
294    NCELL = N * M;
295    if (N < 2) { std::fprintf(stderr, "n must be at least 2\n"); return 1; }
296    if (NCELL > 63) { std::fprintf(stderr, "n*m must be at most 63\n"); return 1; }
297    if (NCELL * 4 > 255) { std::fprintf(stderr, "n*m*4 exceeds 255\n"); return 1; }
298
299    const auto t0 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
300
301    // initial position (the first player occupies the bottom row)
302    State init{ 0, 0, NO_MOVE };
303    for (int c = 0; c < M; c++) {
304        init.cur |= 1ULL << ((N - 1) * M + c);   // the player to move is the first player
305        init.opp |= 1ULL << c;
306    }
307    init = canonical(init);
308
309    Table table;
310    table.init(1 << 20);
311
312    // Nothing is solved here, so neither values nor predecessors are kept; only the
313    // list of representatives.
314    std::vector<State> states;
315
316    auto getId = [&](const State& s, bool& isNew) -> uint32_t {
317        const uint32_t id = (uint32_t)states.size();
318        const uint32_t got = table.findOrInsert(s, id, isNew);
319        if (isNew) states.push_back(s);
320        return got;
321    };
322
323    bool dummy;
324    const uint32_t initId = getId(init, dummy);
